habitat: Small flocks in open bushveld and coastal dune forest, feeding on grass seeds.
summary: A fairly common resident. Red-brown upper parts, black more extensive over the sides of the head and breast than Bronze Mannikin, a uniformly blue-grey bill and broader barring on the flanks. The underparts are white. The immature is duller. It gives a clear whistling note in flight. Newman notes that the red-backed form has been lumped with the black-and-white form despite a colour difference. The short colour line says the bill is white. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Bronze Mannikin is earth-brown above, with black only on the head and breast, a dark upper mandible and fine flank barring. Red-backed Mannikin is red-brown above, with more black and broader flank bars.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^10=1024 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 512–2048.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

head.pattern: Black extends over the sides of the head.

underparts.pattern: Black extends onto the sides of the breast. Broader barring on the flanks.

head.pattern: Duller than the adult. No separate colours were named.

viewNotes.note: Red-brown above, black on the head and sides of the breast, and white below with broad flank bars.
Black face and breast, and a blue-grey bill.
A clear whistling note is given in flight. A wing pattern was not described.
White underparts, with black on the sides of the breast and broader flank barring.

calls.description: A clear whistling note in flight. Grade A call from Obala, Cameroon, labelled Black-and-white Mannikin. The filename says the file was edited. No southern African grade A recording was in the set. Newman treats the red-backed and black-and-white forms as one species.

research.note: The description says the bill is uniformly blue-grey. The short colour line says white. The bill was stored as grey. The recording is the lumped black-and-white form from Cameroon. Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Population figures were left unchanged.
